editor.name: Name
editor.rules_title: Rules (OR — any one matching is enough)
editor.conditions_title: Conditions (AND — every enabled one must match)
editor.verify_modal_hint: 3A writes the network settings, then reads them back and compares. No 3B action starts before that comparison succeeds.
editor.persistent_hint: Each persistent action runs as a worker: it checks the wanted state every interval and only acts when that state is broken. Workers live with Active — leaving this profile stops them.
editor.persistent_else: Persistent actions on the ELSE branch never start — the wanted state only holds while a profile is Active.
editor.none_selected: Select a profile on the left, or create one.
editor.no_rules: No rule: this profile can never match.
editor.actions_hint: 3A must verify successfully before any 3B action runs.
editor.confirm_branch: The engine re-checks this profile's conditions first. Right now that means: {branch}
editor.confirm_dirty: You have unsaved edits — this list comes from the configuration on disk, not from the form.
editor.confirm_3a_none: No 3A: the current network settings stay as they are
editor.confirm_timeout: Each action has its own time limit; exceeding it is reported as a failure, and a running process is never killed.

logs.title: Logs
act.script_denied: the script is not on the allow-list, so it was refused: {path} (resolved to {resolved})
act.thread_died: the action thread exited without handing back a result
act.timeout: no result after {secs}s, so waiting stopped (the action may still be running)
act.check_thread_died: the check thread exited without handing back a result
act.tick_overlap: the previous check (budget {secs}s) had not finished, so this pass was skipped
act.check_timeout: no result after {secs}s, so waiting stopped (the check may still be running)
net.verify_failed: read-back verification still did not match after {tries} samples: {detail}
net.mismatch_missing: {field}: expected {want}, but nothing could be read back
net.dhcp_no_ipv4: DHCP was expected to have leased an IPv4 address, but there is none
upd.no_brew: brew was not found: the Homebrew install method needs Homebrew installed first
cfg.schema_missing: config.json has no top-level "schema" field (this version needs "schema": {schema}). It is not guessed: add the field by following config.example.json.
cfg.schema_unknown: config.json declares schema={found}, which this version does not understand (it needs schema={schema}). Auto-migrating is refused on purpose: other schemas may not read multiple simultaneous matches the way this one does (conflict, apply nothing), and applying a guessed semantics to a network interface is worse than stopping. Check your file against config.example.json.
cfg.no_rules: profile '{name}' has no rules — a profile without rules never matches; disable it or delete it
cfg.rule_no_id: profile '{name}' has a rule with no id
cfg.rule_empty: rule '{rule}' in profile '{name}' is empty — an empty rule never matches; delete it or add conditions
cfg.warn_else_persistent: profile '{name}' configures {count} persistent actions on the else branch: workers only start with the Active profile's then branch, so this branch is never maintained
cfg.cond_no_id: profile '{name}' has a condition with no id
cfg.cond_empty_value: condition '{id}' ({type}) in profile '{name}' has no value — disable it, or fill in the value to compare
cfg.cond_not_mac: condition '{id}' in profile '{name}' needs a MAC-shaped value (current: {value})
cfg.health_icmp: {what}: health probe mode=icmp has no icmp_target
cfg.health_http: {what}: health probe mode=http has no http_target
cfg.health_both: {what}: health probe mode=both needs at least one probe target
cfg.health_interval: {what}: health probe interval must be greater than 0
cfg.health_retries: {what}: health probe retries must be greater than 0 (0 can never be judged a failure)
cfg.health_timeout: {what}: health probe timeout must be greater than 0
cfg.action_needs_both: {what}: action '{id}' is keep_vpn_connected — both provider and profile are required
cfg.net_bad_ip: {what}: ip is not a valid IPv4 address: {ip}
cfg.net_route_no_dest: {what}: a route has an empty dest
cfg.net_route_no_gw: {what}: route {dest} needs a gateway (only a deleted route may omit it)
pal.wait_privileged_failed: cannot wait for the privileged helper: {error}
pal.manual_missing: mode=manual cannot be applied: {field} is missing
pal.v6_manual_missing: v6mode=manual cannot be applied: {field} is missing
pal.v6prefix_range: v6prefix is outside the valid range (0-128): {n}
pal.v6prefix_not_int: v6prefix must be an integer from 0 to 128, received: {s}
pal.no_wifi_service: no Wi-Fi network service was found
pal.no_wifi_device_hint: no Wi-Fi device was found — check that NetworkManager and Wi-Fi are enabled
pal.no_wifi_adapter_hint: no Wi-Fi adapter was found — check that the Wi-Fi adapter is enabled
pal.vpn_iface_not_switchable: interface {dev} is a VPN tunnel: its address is handed out by the VPN client and cannot be switched to DHCP
pal.no_service_for_iface: no network service maps to interface {dev}
pal.xdg_no_args: {app} is not an executable, so only xdg-open can launch it — and xdg-open cannot pass arguments to an app (received {count}). To pass arguments, write app as the absolute path of an executable.
pal.privileged_no_stderr: the privileged script failed and wrote nothing to stderr
pal.scutil_empty: macOS lists no tunnels in its system VPN list (scutil --nc list), so {name} cannot be there
pal.scutil_missing: no tunnel named {name} in the macOS system VPN list; existing: {existing}
pal.scutil_provider_mismatch: the tunnel called {name} in the system VPN list does not match provider={provider}: provider and profile must come from the same tunnel
pal.scutil_start_failed: scutil --nc start {name} failed: {error} (if this is a permission problem, connect it once by hand in System Settings)
pal.nm_up_failed: nmcli connection up {name} failed: {error} (when a password or extra permission is needed, this app will not answer the prompt for you)
pal.sudo_ip_link_failed: sudo -n ip link set {name} up failed: {error}
pal.ip_link_needs_root: kernel interface {name} exists but could not be brought up, and `ip link set up` needs root. This app never raises an authorization dialog in the background: create a NetworkManager connection for that interface, or configure passwordless sudoers.
pal.tunnel_missing_no_nm: no tunnel {name} on Linux: NetworkManager has no connections at all, and the kernel has no device by that name
pal.tunnel_missing_nm_list: no tunnel {name} on Linux; NetworkManager already has: {conns}
pal.tunnel_name_invalid: {name} is not a valid tunnel name: it must be the tunnel's own name, with no path separators or control characters
pal.no_programdata: %PROGRAMDATA% was not found, so WireGuard's tunnel configuration directory cannot be located
pal.wg_dir_empty: the WireGuard configuration directory ({dir}) has no tunnels at all — import a tunnel named {name} in the WireGuard client first
pal.wg_conf_missing: there is no {name}.conf in the WireGuard configuration directory; installed tunnels: {existing}
pal.wg_install_failed: {exe} /installtunnelservice {conf} failed: {error} (installing the tunnel service needs administrator rights, and this app does not raise UAC in the background)
pal.rasdial_failed: rasdial {entry} failed: {error} (a connection that needs a credential or code entered by hand cannot be dialed in the background — connect it once manually and tick the option to save the credentials)
pal.iface_provider_mismatch: the description of adapter {name} ({desc}) does not indicate provider={provider}: provider and profile must come from the same tunnel
pal.iface_missing_wg: there is no network adapter named {name} on Windows; WireGuard tunnels installed: {conns}
pal.iface_missing_none: there is no network adapter named {name} on Windows (this machine has no tunnels installed at all)
